title: vLLM late-interaction query-cache key collision
summary: When flash late-interaction scoring is enabled, vLLM derives query-embedding cache keys from caller-controlled request IDs. Concurrent requests that share an identifier can collide in the cache, letting one request use another request’s query embeddings and corrupt scoring results or cause errors.
ai_role: The vLLM project advisory explicitly states that this vulnerability was discovered using GPT-5.5-Cyber as part of the Patch the Planet security initiative. This establishes AI-enabled discovery attribution; the source does not establish model autonomy or the private discovery date.
classification_note: The advisory establishes public disclosure and the documented fix scope. It does not establish whether defenders knew of the issue or whether it was exploited before disclosure.
remediation_note: vLLM versions below 0.30.0 are affected; 0.30.0 and later are listed as patched. The advisory links proposed fix PR #51445; the exact earliest affected release is not established.

impacts.conditions: Requires a deployment with flash late-interaction scoring enabled, concurrent requests sharing a caller-controlled request ID, and the attacker knowing or selecting the victim identifier; the affected endpoints are /score and /rerank.
impacts.exploitation: The advisory describes reproducible conditions but does not report observed exploitation.
